transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t get this thought out of my head. I’ve been an electrician for years, and if I couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then… I don’t know. It feels like I’m a danger to anyone working with me, or anyone living under my roof.
Can you tell me more about that thought — what exactly are you thinking or imagining when you say you can’t get it out of your head?

It’s… mostly this one idea. Like, I should’ve known better. I’ve done electrical work for years, and if I couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then maybe I’m just… not safe to be around. Not at a job, not at home. Like anyone near me could get hurt because of me.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or worthless about this situation with your brother, even if you know logically it might not be your fault?

Yeah… I do. I know people say it wasn’t all on me, but it doesn’t feel that way.

It’s just this heavy mix of guilt and anger that sits there all day. Especially when I look at my nephew and think… he lost his dad, and got stuck with me instead.
Have you noticed these feelings of guilt and worthlessness about your brother’s situation happening most days, and do they seem excessive even beyond what the situation calls for?

Yeah… most days. It’s kind of just there.

I know maybe it’s more than what makes sense, but it doesn’t feel that way. It’s this guilt and anger sitting in my chest all day… and when I look at my nephew, I just think he lost his dad and got stuck with me instead.
Over the past few weeks, have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or found yourself feeling down or hopeless most of the time?

I don’t know… I haven’t really thought about it like that.

I’m not exactly enjoying much, but I don’t know if I’d call it hopeless. I’m just… getting through the days, I guess.
Have you found that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in doing things you once liked?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I don’t do much lately, but I can’t say if it’s because I don’t enjoy it or just because I don’t feel like dealing with anything.
Can you think of something you used to enjoy, even a little, like a hobby or time with family? If you did, have you found yourself not caring about that anymore?

I don’t know. Maybe stuff around the house, watching a game with family… things like that.

I haven’t really paid attention to whether I care or not. I just don’t end up doing much.
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed that you don’t get any enjoyment or pleasure from things you used to like, even a little bit?
I’m… not sure. I haven’t really noticed it that clearly. I don’t go out of my way to do those things much, but I can’t say if there’s no pleasure there or if I’m just not trying.

Can you think back to any activity or moment where you used to feel enjoyment, even something small—like a hobby, a show, or time with someone? Have you felt any of that enjoyment lately, even a little?
I don’t know… maybe watching something or being around family, but I can’t really tell you I felt much from it. I haven’t paid close enough attention, I guess. I mostly just… get through it.
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed that you don’t get any enjoyment or pleasure from things you used to like, even a little bit?
I can’t really say. I haven’t noticed it in a clear way. I know I don’t do much of that stuff anymore, but whether I’m not enjoying it or just not paying attention… I don’t know.
Looking back, would you say you’ve completely lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, even ones you did just for a little fun or relaxation?
I don’t know if I’d say completely. I mean… I don’t really do much of it anymore, but I can’t tell if the interest is gone or if I just don’t bother. Hard to say.
Looking at the past few weeks, would you say you’ve experienced little to no interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even ones you did just for a little fun or relaxation?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track of it like that. I know I don’t do much for fun lately, but whether that means I don’t enjoy it… I can’t say for sure.
Looking back, have you felt any interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even small things like watching a show or being around family?
I don’t really know. Maybe here and there, but I haven’t… paid much attention to whether I’m actually enjoying it or just sitting through it.
Looking back over the past two weeks, would you say that you’ve taken little or no pleasure in all or most of your usual activities, even ones you used to enjoy?
I’m not sure I’d put it that strongly. I mean, I haven’t really been doing much, but… whether it’s no pleasure in most things, I don’t know. I haven’t really thought it through like that.
Looking back over the past two weeks, would you say that you’ve taken little or no pleasure in most of your usual activities, even ones you used to enjoy?
I don’t really know. I guess I haven’t noticed much pleasure, but I can’t say if it’s most things or not. I just haven’t been paying attention to it like that.
Looking back over the past two weeks, would you say that you’ve taken little or no pleasure in most of your usual activities, even ones you used to enjoy?
I don’t know. I mean… maybe, but I haven’t really been keeping track of it. Most things just kind of happen and I get through them.
Looking back, can you say that there were at least two weeks in a row where you felt little interest or pleasure in most activities you used to enjoy, even things you did just for fun or relaxation?
I… I can’t really say that for sure. There’ve been stretches where I didn’t feel much, but whether it was two weeks straight or most activities… I don’t know.
Looking back, can you say that there was a period of at least two weeks where you felt no interest or pleasure in almost anything you used to enjoy?
I don’t know that I can say “almost anything.” There were times I didn’t feel much interest, yeah, but pinning it down to two weeks like that… I’m not sure.
Looking back, can you say that there was a time when, for at least two weeks in a row, you felt no interest or pleasure in nearly everything you used to enjoy doing?
I don’t think I can say that, no. Not clearly. I’ve had times where I didn’t care much about things, but “nearly everything” for two weeks straight… I’m not sure.

F43.22 (Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood) remains relevant given the reaction to a psychosocial stressor (the brother’s death and its aftermath).

The patient continues to endorse persistent guilt, worthlessness, and ruminations about past events, which supports the continuation of F32.3 (Major Depressive Disorder, recurrent, severe) and F43.22 (Adjustment Disorder with Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood).
